result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, so post.cook returns raw unfiltered (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in post.rb). Readability whitelist includes `attributes: %w[href src]` for a/img, and absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with '/', so `javascript:` URLs pass through unchanged and are rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view, which is served from the Discourse origin (X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL iframe). Imported javascript: links thus execute on the Discourse origin when clicked.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method that bypasses the rendering/sanitization pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which only rewrites `href`/`src` values that start with `/` and leaves other schemes untouched. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses Readability with `attributes: %w[href src]` but no scheme filtering is shown in the diff. The embed view renders the cooked content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so an imported `<a href='javascript:...'>` would remain and be rendered as-is inside the Discourse-served iframe, enabling script execution on click. This is a verifiable XSS/vector introduced by the raw HTML import path in this diff.
